relevance_note: Single case report of a boy with a clinical (MRI-based) diagnosis of Alexander disease: "Our child was diagnosed as AD in view of macrocephaly, seizures, developmental delay in a young child with MRI findings"; no GFAP variant reported because "GFAP was not available".
method_note: Read by hand; JSON assembled with a short Python script from values chosen while reading. One in-scope person (rule 5 label 'patient'), in scope by diagnosis of Alexander disease only; GFAP analysis was not done ('GFAP was not available'), so no variants rows. n_patients_reported left null because no patient with a GFAP variant is described. first_author recorded as 'Kumar' from the header 'Kumar K. Jagadish' (surname-first ordering inferred from the other author entries such as 'Manjunath V. G.'). Age at onset taken from the first seizure at 5 months; the paper gives no explicit onset age for the developmental delay. No age at diagnosis stated. 'Examination of other systems was unremarkable' and 'no family history of seizures or neurological illness' were not turned into feature rows (general/relatives). Normal lab panel recorded per D-27 as excluded abnormalities, one row per named test. 'cranial nerves were normal' was not used to exclude the checklist item eye movement abnormality (general normal finding). MRI was 'with contrast' but enhancement is not described, so contrast enhancement is not reported. Spasticity/pyramidal signs marked observed from brisk reflexes with bilateral plantar extensors, although tone was stated normal. Discussion mention of status epilepticus 'reported by others also.[7]' gives no individual-level fact, so no row. No contradictions found.
